name: Senir's Observations
summary: This errand completes a scouting line out of Coldridge Valley, carrying Grelin Whitebeard's completed report through the trogg-infested pass to his brother Senir in Kharanos. It bridges the secluded training grounds of Anvilmar with the broader troubles facing Dun Morogh. Through Senir's candid reception, travelers catch their first glimpse of political friction simmering between field scouts and the Ironforge Senate.

sections.title: Through the Tunnel to Kharanos
sections.body: After Grelin Whitebeard recovers his stolen journal from the Frostmane trolls, he prepares a detailed report of the valley's threats for his brother Senir. Mountaineer Thalos, stationed guarding the gate out of Coldridge Valley, entrusts passing adventurers with carrying this dispatch. Leaving the relative seclusion of the introductory vale means braving the tunnel cut through the mountain, which has recently been overrun by violent troggs ambushing all traffic. Travelers who punch through emerge onto the snowblown highways of central Dun Morogh, following the main road straight into the cozy hub of Kharanos.

sections.title: A Grumpy Welcome and Senate Politics
sections.body: Senir Whitebeard, found seeking warmth over drinks at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, greets newcomers with rough mountaineer hospitality. Reading through Grelin's findings, Senir chuckles over his brother's aggressive rhetoric. Grelin liberally invokes the name of King Magni Bronzebeard to press for urgent action, an assertive tactic Senir notes is bound to agitate the stubborn Ironforge Senate. Senir admits he has fallen behind on filing his own observations due to the bitter cold, but receiving Grelin's dispatch nudges him back into service, opening further work monitoring hostile forces across the snowfields.

faq.q: Why is Mountaineer Thalos having a traveler deliver the report?
faq.answer: Mountaineer Thalos is posted to hold the defense line at the Coldridge Valley tunnel against aggressive troggs. He cannot abandon his watchpost, so when an able adventurer comes through, he tasks them with carrying Grelin's dispatch safely into Kharanos.
Senir Whitebeard is a dwarven scout and brother to Grelin Whitebeard. Stationed at Kharanos, he collates scouting field reports on local threats to pass along to the high command in Ironforge.

The report compiles Grelin's findings on the Frostmane troll activity and incursions within Coldridge Valley. Written urgently, it invokes King Magni Bronzebeard's authority to demand reinforcements and attention from the authorities.

faq.q: Why does Senir say Grelin's report will ruffle feathers in the Senate?
faq.answer: Grelin invokes King Magni's name forcefully to demand action. In Ironforge politics, relying on royal decrees can bypass or challenge the bureaucratic authority and pride of the dwarven Senate, irritating council members who prefer formal deliberation.

faq.q: Why is the tunnel between Coldridge Valley and Kharanos dangerous?
aliases: why are troggs in the tunnel
faq.answer: A clan of Rockjaw troggs has recently emerged from the deep subterranean cracks and seized the mountain tunnel, attacking any dwarven travelers, merchants, or messengers trying to pass through.

faq.q: Where does the road lead after delivering this message?
faq.answer: Arriving in Kharanos integrates adventurers into the broader defense of Dun Morogh. Senir Whitebeard later enlists help investigating further Frostmane and trogg threats, while town leaders direct aid toward Brewnall Village, Ironforge, and the outlying farms.

angles.text: Passing from the sheltered training valley into Kharanos marks your true graduation into the defense of Khaz Modan, offering an early taste of how field scouts clash with Ironforge's cautious Senate.
Heading through the pass to Kharanos brings exiled gnomes closer to the main hubs of Dun Morogh and the ongoing efforts to support their dwarven hosts.
Helping scouts coordinate intelligence keeps Dun Morogh secure at a time when Stormwind is paralyzed by domestic strife and cannot spare aid for its northern allies.
